analysis:
The change only touches scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py. It adds `import shutil` (head line 5) and a new ReleaseCMakeTests class (head lines 66-117). The class exercises scripts/install-release-cmake.sh with stubbed uname and curl in a temporary directory, covering three cases: a complete tool-cache CMake of the exact version is used without downloading; an absent, incomplete or wrong-version cache falls back to a download; and a failed download leaves PATH untouched and the step fails. This is test-only code. It adds no runtime provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache or inference behavior, so none of the threat-model assets, boundaries or threats are altered (T-041 and TB-007 are not affected).

The tests run offline with a stubbed curl, so there is no network access. Temp directories are created with tempfile and cleaned up. `shutil.rmtree(ignore_errors=True)` only targets the test's own tempdir cache. The tests do show that the production script trusts an `universal.complete` marker plus a `cmake --version` output string from RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE, which is a runner-image trust assumption. The script itself is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not check the download integrity verification (checksum or signature) or how a tool-cache binary is validated beyond its version output. This belongs to supply-chain and build-pipeline review, not to this test diff, and I did not treat it as a finding. The next pass should examine scripts/install-release-cmake.sh if it appears in another batch, checking for a pinned hash on the download and whether a self-hosted runner's tool cache is attacker-writable.
